title: True Mysteries of the Internet
summary: Josh and Chuck cover three unsolved Internet mysteries. First, Cicada 3301: the 2012 multi-step online puzzle that started on 4chan, involving steganography, a Caesar cipher, a phone number, GPS coordinates on telephone poles, and a final website; solvers such as Marcus Wanner and Joel Erickson are mentioned, and the group's motives remain unclear. Second, the most mysterious song on the Internet: an unidentified early-1980s synthpop/post-punk track taped off German radio (Radio DDR-style music program) by Darius S. onto a cassette, with spectrogram and synthesizer analysis dating it to 1983-84 and no one identifying the artist. Third, John Titor: an internet poster who claimed to be a time traveler from 2036, whose posts began via faxes read on Art Bell's Coast to Coast AM and continued on the Time Travel Institute site; the IBM 5100 detail and Tipler's time machine concept are discussed, and investigators point to Florida and the Haber family as possible authors. The episode closes with a listener mail tomato fact about lead plates and tomatoes.

segments.title: Cicada 3301
segments.summary: The 2012 Cicada 3301 puzzle series posted on 4chan, its steganography and Caesar cipher steps, the Arthurian legend clues, phone call, prime-number instructions, GPS coordinates and telephone pole QR codes, the shutdown website, solvers Marcus Wanner and Joel Erickson, and theories about who was behind it.

segments.title: The most mysterious song on the Internet
segments.summary: An unidentified early-1980s synthpop track taped off German radio by Darius S.; his sister Lydia H. pushed to identify it; spectrogram analysis tied it to a radio station's modulation line, a Yamaha DX7 suggested a 1983-84 date, playlists and DJ Paul Baskerville did not resolve it, and the hosts offer theories including the artist having died unknown.

segments.title: John Titor time traveler mystery
segments.summary: The John Titor posts starting from faxes read on Art Bell's Coast to Coast AM and the Time Travel Institute site, claims of a 2036 time traveler, the IBM 5100 detail, Tipler's theory, his farewell post, and investigations pointing to the Haber family in Florida and Joseph Matheny's claim to have started it.

segments.title: Listener mail: tomatoes and lead
